### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **1** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 39 pages)`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab7599665631c2da6736c6c48abcf3dea5221575` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

Addendum to the handoff above, for ④ on head ecf8b5c4

The epic PM weighed whether admitting `user` on the `text` row is a design decision outside the card. I judge that it is not. Rulings 6512853588 and 6512860835 (option A on #27745) made `lookup` / `master_detail` exact on text, integer and bigint rows. The matrix judges column storage shape against the field's value shape, and `user` is a lookup whose target id (`sys_user.id`) is always a string. The card names this outcome as the measured one. Integer rows stay refused for `user`, so the PR applies the ruling's principle and widens nothing past it.

Please judge one point explicitly in ④. An external table's text column holds the external system's user keys, not platform `sys_user` ids, so a `user` field there type-checks but may not resolve. Is that the same, already-accepted shape-only contract `lookup` has to a platform object (in which case PASS on this point)? Or does `user` need the matrix to refuse it, or the PR to state the non-resolution, as a must-fix?

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ecf8b5c41d1e456f079d87b0d9542caa998ca7b5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/type-compat.ts, docs/adr/0015-external-datasource-federation.md + packages/services/service-datasource/src/external-datasource-service.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/objectql-adapter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/src/mongodb-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/data/type-compat.test.ts, .changeset/27917-type-compat-user-text.md

Inputs: card #27917 (body, claim 6516916650, os-dev-report 6517630083), PR #28011 (body, file list, net diff of four files against `main`), the handoff 6517644210 and addendum 6517664760, and the 55 check-runs on this head. The remainder of the diff (`type-compat.test.ts`, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; both were read to judge the `hits` files, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged against the live tree:

- `isCompatible(column, 'user', dialect)` turns from `false` to `true` for every column that canonicalises to `text`: the base aliases (`text`, `varchar`, `char`, `character`, `string`, `character varying`, `nvarchar`, `nchar`, `clob`), postgres `bpchar` / `citext`, mysql `tinytext` / `mediumtext` / `longtext`, sqlite `text`, snowflake `string` / `varchar`, bigquery `string`, mongo `objectid` / `string`, odata `edm.string`. **Right.** `field.zod.ts` declares the `user` type "stored IDENTICALLY to 'lookup' (FK string column → sys_user.id)" (lines 82-89 and the `Field.user` helper), and the platform's own `sys_user.id` column is `table.string('id').primary()`, i.e. `varchar(255)` (`sql-driver.ts` lines 10457 and 10550). The `text` row is therefore the platform's OWN physical shape for a user id, the same ground the row's existing `signature` / `qrcode` comment stands on. The `mongo.objectid` consequence (a Mongo ObjectId column typed `user` now passes) is the same shape-only contract `lookup` already has on that alias.
- `isCompatible(column, 'user')` stays `false` on the `integer` and `bigint` rows (`Edm.Int32`, `Edm.Int64`, `int8`, mysql `int`, bigquery `int64` and the rest), while `lookup` / `master_detail` stay exact there. **Right.** A federated `lookup`'s target id is the remote key, so a remote integer column can carry it; a `user` field's target is fixed to `sys_user` by the type (`USER_FIELD_TARGET`, `field.zod.ts` lines 2508-2535), whose id column is a `varchar(255)` string on every driver. Nothing in the tree mints a non-string user id; see ③.
- `uuid` row unchanged (`user` was already exact there); `json`, `array`, `enum`, `binary`, `decimal`, `float`, `boolean`, `date`, `time`, `datetime`, `vector`, `unknown` rows unchanged for `user`. **Right** as far as the card reaches. (Observation, not a finding on this diff: a `multiple: true` `user` field stores a JSON array per `field.zod.ts`, and the `json` / `array` rows list neither `user` nor `lookup`; the gap predates this PR and is shared with `lookup`.)
- Gate 2 consequence (`validateObject`, `external-datasource-service.ts` lines 1024-1041): a federated object declaring a `user` field over a text-family column no longer yields a `type_mismatch` diff at severity `error`, so the boot under `onMismatch: 'fail'` no longer refuses it. The widening is monotone: no column/field pair that answered `true` or `'lossy'` before answers less now. **Right.**
- Draft generator unchanged: every row's `suggested` is untouched, so `generateObjectDraft` (lines 778-791) still drafts `text` for a text column and never emits `user`. **Right**, and the new test pins it.
- Public surface: no export added, removed or renamed; `SqlDialect`, `Compatibility`, `canonicalizeSqlType`, `suggestFieldTypeForSqlType` and `isCompatible` keep their signatures; `api-surface/data.json` needs no regeneration and the `TypeScript Type Check` job (which carries `check:api-surface`) is green on this head. **Right.**
- ADR-0015 §4.6: the dialect list now reads `postgres`, `mysql`, `sqlite`, `snowflake`, `bigquery`, `mongo`, `odata`, which equals the seven members of `SqlDialect` at this head. **Right.** The sentence that follows it makes a claim the code it names contradicts; see ④ (must-fix).
- The `Amended by` line records the amendment as "dialect list only". **Right** for the ADR's own change: §4.6 has never enumerated matrix membership (the lookup / master_detail widening of the prior card amended nothing in it either), so the `user` row change is not an ADR decision and needs no ADR line.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and in the changeset. **Right.** `isCompatible` is a published function of `@objectstack/spec/data` (`export * from './type-compat'` in `data/index.ts`; `api-surface/data.json` lists it), and its accept set widens with no signature change. The card's provisional `yes` is restated from the diff as the claim required.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`. **Right.** No authorable key, value or metadata type changes: `FieldTypeSchema` and the `user` type's keys are untouched. What moves is a boot-time gate's verdict over a remote schema, not what an author can write.
- `.changeset/27917-type-compat-user-text.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch, both declaration lines present. **Right level.** A `none` protocol kind takes patch, and a non-protocol widening ships patch. The changeset's prose matches the diff (text row gains `user`; integer rows unchanged; §4.6 lists `odata`). `Check Changeset` is green on this head.
- No `skip-changeset`; nothing else publishes (`docs/adr/**` is not a package).

### ③ Boundary flags

- os-dev-report 6517630083: `open_questions: []`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`. Nothing to answer.
- PR acceptance note "Memory and Mongo drivers mint their own ids for engine-direct writes; those were not measured." **Answered here.** `driver-memory` mints the string `` `${objectName}-${Date.now()}-${counter}` `` (`memory-driver.ts` lines 2646-2652); `driver-mongodb` mints `nanoid(DEFAULT_ID_LENGTH)` (`mongodb-driver.ts` lines 415-416, 487-488, 548). Both strings. Closed.
- PR acceptance note "Integer rows left closed by measurement, not by caution." **Answered, and the ground is firmer than the PR states.** The platform's own `sys_user.id` column is `varchar(255)` on every SQL dialect (`sql-driver.ts` line 10550, and the comment at line 10457 records the live PostgreSQL reading). A seeded user (`app-plugin.ts` around line 2102 inserts seed rows straight through `engine.insert`) may supply any id, which the driver stores verbatim or replaces with a 16-character nanoid (`sql-driver.ts` lines 6459-6464); either way it is a string in a text-shaped column. So the closure rests on the platform's column shape, not only on the minters' output. Closed.
- The measurement itself ("better-auth 1.7.12 mints a 32-character alphanumeric id; admin create and import share the path"). **Judged against the producers on `main`, not re-run (read-only).** `plugin-auth/package.json` pins `better-auth` at `1.7.12`; `objectql-adapter.ts` builds the adapter through `createAdapterFactory` with `adapterId`, `supportsBooleans`, `supportsDates`, `supportsJSON` and `transaction` only (lines 885-915), no `customIdGenerator`; the `advanced` block of `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts` (lines 827-838) carries cookies, CSRF and the client-address source, no `database.generateId`; so the library default applies, and the dev's five-sample reading is consistent with that default's documented shape. `admin-import-users.ts` line 715 and `admin-user-endpoints.ts` line 812 both call `authApi.createUser`, the same id path. IdP-provisioned (SSO JIT) and SCIM identities arrive through the same adapter `create`. No path in the tree mints an integer user id. Closed.
- Epic PM addendum 6517664760 (does an external text column that holds the remote system's user keys, which type-checks but may not resolve, need a refusal or a stated non-resolution?). **Answered in ④: PASS on the point, no fix owed.**
- "Review owed" (PR body and handoff). This record is the at-tier contract review on this head and, per the handoff and the standing order of 2026-10-29, also serves as the full review of the spec and ADR change. Tier H landing still needs an authorized APPROVE from `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` on top of a PASS record; the PR stays draft until then. On this head the verdict is FAIL (④), so nothing is readied.
- Observation for the lane, outside ④ (PR prose is not reviewed): the PR body's review-owed sentence names models by marketing name, which the repo's rule on model identifiers forbids in a PR body; the dispatch claim prescribed that phrasing, so the conflict is the lane's to settle, not a finding on the `hits` files.
- Check-runs on this head: 55, all completed, none failed. The gate-carrying required contexts are `success` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` and all eight shards, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`); `Lint UI` is skipped by its path filter; `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `PR-body guards` and `Docs Drift Check` are `success`. The gate verdicts are green; the FAIL below is a ④ finding the gates do not measure.
- `origin/main` has moved past the branch point; the one `main` commit since then that touches `service-datasource` (the connector-credential verdict, #27990) edits `datasource-connection-service.ts` only, not the matrix's consumer `validateObject`. No overlap with the `hits` files.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/type-compat.ts` — against the ruling it applies and its first consumer. Holds.**

- Scenario accepted against: a federated object declaring a `user` field over a text-family column boots instead of failing Gate 2 with a `type_mismatch` error; the same field over an integer column still fails. Read in `validateObject` (lines 1024-1041): the only reader that refuses is this one, keyed on `isCompatible(col.type, fieldType, dialect)`; the row change produces exactly that pair of outcomes, and the new test (`type-compat.test.ts` lines 186-209) pins both sides across base, postgres, bigquery and odata spellings plus the `lookup` contrast on the same integer columns.
- Against the ruling (option A on the prior card: `lookup` / `master_detail` exact on text, integer and bigint): the matrix judges a column's storage shape against the field's value shape. `user` is a lookup whose target is fixed to `sys_user`; the platform's id column is `varchar(255)`; so `text` is its exact row and the integer rows are not. The PR applies the ruling's principle and widens nothing past it. Not a design decision outside the card: the card named this outcome as the measured one and set the condition for the integer rows, which the measurement does not meet.
- Attempts to break it: (a) a `multiple: true` `user` field stores a JSON array, which no text column carries exactly; but the `json` row lists neither `user` nor `lookup`, the gap predates this diff and is shared with `lookup`, so it is not this PR's. (b) A caller-supplied id can be a UUID or digit-only string; the `uuid` row keeps `user`, and a digit-only string is still a string in a `varchar(255)` column, so the integer rows' refusal stays honest. (c) `mongo.objectid` canonicalises to `text`, so an ObjectId column typed `user` now passes; same shape-only contract `lookup` already has there. None breaks the row.
- The epic PM's explicit question. An external table whose text column holds the REMOTE system's user keys, declared `user`, type-checks and may not resolve. **This is the same, already-accepted shape-only contract `lookup` has, so PASS on this point.** Three reasons. First, the matrix is keyed on the column and judges shape, never provenance: a `Field.lookup('account')` on a federated row whose column holds the remote CRM's account key type-checks and may not resolve in exactly the same way, and that is the accepted contract since the prior ruling. Second, the same non-resolution class already existed on `main` for `user` under the `uuid` row (a remote GUID column typed `user`); this diff extends the row set to where the platform's id actually lives, it does not create the class. Third, a matrix refusal would also refuse the legitimate case the card is about (an external table that mirrors platform user ids), and by shape the matrix cannot tell the two apart in either row. Declaring `user` is the author's claim that the column holds platform user ids; the row comment states that contract ("the column holds a PLATFORM user id"), and a dangling reference resolves to nothing through the same expand path a dangling `lookup` does. No rule requires the PR to state the non-resolution further, and no refusal is owed.
- **Should-fix (comment precision, not a FAIL):** the row comment says the id is "a string either way, never a UUID and never an integer". "Never a UUID" is true of the minters only; a caller-supplied id (a seed row, an `_id`) is stored verbatim, which is exactly why the `uuid` row keeps `user`. One clause: "the minted id is never a UUID or an integer; a caller-supplied id is stored verbatim as a string, which is why the uuid row keeps user".

**`docs/adr/0015-external-datasource-federation.md` — against its first consumer (the `odata` arm and the `SqlDialect` vocabulary in `type-compat.ts`) and its execution plan. Does not hold on one clause.**

- The dialect list: now `postgres`, `mysql`, `sqlite`, `snowflake`, `bigquery`, `mongo`, `odata`, equal to `SqlDialect`'s seven members at this head. Holds. The card's first task is met.
- The pointer: "its aliases (`DIALECT_ALIASES.odata`)" names the module-private table the arm lives in, which is what the card asked for, and the arm's own comment ("OData's EDM primitives (CSDL 4.0 §4.4)") agrees with the ADR's description of what it maps. Holds.
- The `Amended by` entry: dated, scoped to the dialect list, pointing at the prior card that brought the arm. Holds.
- **Must-fix (FAIL):** the sentence added to §4.6 reads "`odata` is the one vocabulary that is not SQL". The code it names says otherwise: the `SqlDialect` doc comment at the top of `type-compat.ts` reads "SQL dialects, plus the two non-SQL ones a federation driver reports (`mongo`'s BSON types, `odata`'s EDM primitives)", and the `mongo` arm beside the `odata` arm maps BSON type names (`objectid`, `bindata`, `long`, `bool`). The amendment therefore writes into a governed record an exclusive claim that the cited code contradicts, on the very sentence whose purpose is to make §4.6 agree with that code. The card exists because the last record's should-fixes were not taken into their PR; landing a known-false sentence in a Tier H ADR and filing a third follow-up is worse than the one-sentence fix. Fix: "`mongo` and `odata` are the two vocabularies that are not SQL: `DIALECT_ALIASES.mongo` maps BSON type names, and `DIALECT_ALIASES.odata` maps the EDM primitive types an OData service's `$metadata` declares." The `odata` pointer the card asked for stays.
- **Should-fix (fold into the same sentence):** "map the EDM primitive types an OData service's `$metadata` declares" reads as all of them; the arm deliberately leaves `Edm.Duration` and the `Edm.Geography*` / `Edm.Geometry*` families unmapped so a draft flags them for review (the arm's own comment). Either "maps the EDM primitive types the arm's comment lists" or a trailing "(duration and the geography / geometry families are left unmapped for review)".

Verdict reasoning: one must-fix on a `hits` file is a FAIL. The `type-compat.ts` change holds against its ruling, its spec and its first consumer, and the gate verdicts are green; the next head needs only the §4.6 sentence corrected (and may take the two should-fixes), after which a PASS record on that head goes to an approver.
